question: Which of the following vaccines is correctly matched with its classification?

answers.text: BCG — live attenuated; OPV — live attenuated; Hepatitis B — recombinant subunit

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. BCG and OPV (oral polio vaccine) are live attenuated vaccines; the Hepatitis B vaccine is a recombinant subunit vaccine (HBsAg produced in yeast).

answers.text: BCG — killed; OPV — live attenuated; Hepatitis B — toxoid

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. BCG (Bacille Calmette-Guérin) is a live attenuated bacterial vaccine, not a killed vaccine. Hepatitis B is a recombinant subunit vaccine, not a toxoid.

answers.text: BCG — live attenuated; IPV — live attenuated; Hepatitis B — recombinant subunit

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. IPV (inactivated polio vaccine) is a killed/inactivated vaccine, not live attenuated. OPV is the live attenuated polio vaccine.

answers.text: BCG — live attenuated; OPV — inactivated; Hepatitis B — live attenuated

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. OPV is a live attenuated vaccine (Sabin), not inactivated. Hepatitis B is a recombinant subunit vaccine.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the Classification block. Key rule: live vaccines (BCG, OPV, MMR, varicella) are contraindicated in immunocompromised patients; inactivated and subunit vaccines are generally safe.
Excellent. Correctly classifying vaccines is foundational for understanding their cold chain requirements, contraindications in immunocompromised patients, and scheduling rules.
